english_paragraphs: Charles Darwin disembarked from HMS Beagle in October 1836. In September 1838 he began formulating the principle of natural selection: individuals better adapted to their surroundings survive and pass on their hereditary traits. By 1844 he had composed a 230-page manuscript, yet kept it unpublished, cautiously amassing evidence.

In February 1858, two decades after Darwin's first insight, Alfred Russel Wallace, a naturalist afflicted by fever in the Malay Archipelago, independently conceived the same idea. His concise essay reached Darwin on 18 June 1858. Its argument paralleled Darwin's own almost precisely; he told Charles Lyell he had never seen a more remarkable coincidence. His claim to priority seemed threatened.

Lyell and the botanist Joseph Hooker arranged for both papers to be read simultaneously at the Linnean Society, a scientific institution in London, on 1 July 1858. Neither author attended the proceedings. Wallace was abroad, and Darwin was grieving: scarlet fever had killed his infant son on 28 June. The compromise, struck without Wallace, may have kept rivalry over precedence at bay.

The papers' publication on 20 August 1858 met a muted reception. In May 1859 the Society's president remarked in his yearly address that the year had been barren of revolutionary discoveries. The sensation came on 24 November 1859 with Darwin's treatise, On the Origin of Species: booksellers had subscribed for every copy of its first impression, 1,250 in all.

Wallace had readily signified his acceptance in October 1858, assuring Hooker in a cordial letter of his satisfaction with the arrangement. In 1889 he published a lengthy exposition of the idea and entitled it Darwinism. Wallace never named the theory after himself.
chinese_source_paragraphs: 1836年10月，查尔斯·达尔文从小猎犬号上**登岸**(disembarked)。1838年9月，他开始**构想并明确表述**(formulating)自然**选择**(selection)的**原理**(principle)：**对**(adapted to)**周围环境**(surroundings)**适应**(adapted to)得更好的个体存活下来，并将**传递**(pass on)他们自身**遗传的**(hereditary)**性状**(traits)（给后代）。到1844年，他已**撰写了**(composed)一份230页的**手稿**(manuscript)，却一直**未予发表**(unpublished)，**谨慎地**(cautiously)**积累着**(amassing)证据。

1858年2月，达尔文最初的洞察出现后的二十年，**博物学家**(naturalist)阿尔弗雷德·拉塞尔·华莱士在马来群岛**饱受**(afflicted by)热病**的折磨**(afflicted by)，**独自一人**(independently)**构想出**(conceived)了同一个想法。华莱士这篇**简明的**(concise)文章于1858年6月18日到达了达尔文的手里。文中的论证**与**(paralleled)达尔文自己的几乎**完全**(precisely)**一样**(paralleled)；达尔文告诉查尔斯·莱尔，自己从未见过比这更**惊人的**(remarkable)**巧合**(coincidence)。他对**优先权**(priority)的主张似乎**受到了威胁**(threatened)。

莱尔和**植物学家**(botanist)约瑟夫·胡克**安排**(arranged for)这两篇论文，于1858年7月1日在伦敦的科学**机构**(institution)林奈学会上被**同时**(simultaneously)宣读。两位作者都没有出席这场**会议**(proceedings)。华莱士身在海外，达尔文则处于**哀痛**(grieving)之中：**猩红**(scarlet)热在6月28日夺去了他**幼子**(infant)的生命。这一**折中办法**(compromise)在华莱士未参与的情况下达成，或许避免了围绕**先后次序**(precedence)的**竞争**(rivalry)。

这些论文于1858年8月20日的**发表**(publication)，遭遇了一个**很不热烈的**(muted)**反响**(reception)。1859年5月，学会会长在**年度**(yearly)致辞中**评论**(remarked)说，这一年一直**毫无**(barren of)**革命性的**(revolutionary)发现。这场**轰动**(sensation)于1859年11月24日随着达尔文的**专著**(treatise)**《物种起源》**(On the Origin of Species)到来：书商们已**订购了**(subscribed for)该书首**次印刷**(impression)的每一册，总计1,250册。

华莱士早已**欣然**(readily)**表明了**(signified)**接受**(acceptance)的态度，那是在1858年10月；他在一封**亲切的**(cordial)信中**向**(assuring)胡克**保证**(assuring)，自己对这一**安排**(arrangement)感到**满意**(satisfaction)。1889年，他出版了一部**长篇的**(lengthy)**阐述**(exposition)解释这一思想，并**将**(entitled)其**命名为**(entitled)《达尔文主义》。华莱士从未**用**(named after)自己的名字**为**(named after)这一理论**命名**(named after)。

sentences.english: In May 1859 the Society's president remarked in his yearly address that the year had been barren of revolutionary discoveries.
sentences.chinese_source: 1859年5月，学会会长在**年度**(yearly)致辞中**评论**(remarked)说，这一年一直**毫无**(barren of)**革命性的**(revolutionary)发现。

sentences.english: The sensation came on 24 November 1859 with Darwin's treatise, On the Origin of Species: booksellers had subscribed for every copy of its first impression, 1,250 in all.
sentences.chinese_source: 这场**轰动**(sensation)于1859年11月24日随着达尔文的**专著**(treatise)**《物种起源》**(On the Origin of Species)到来：书商们已**订购了**(subscribed for)该书首**次印刷**(impression)的每一册，总计1,250册。

sentences.english: Wallace had readily signified his acceptance in October 1858, assuring Hooker in a cordial letter of his satisfaction with the arrangement.
sentences.chinese_source: 华莱士早已**欣然**(readily)**表明了**(signified)**接受**(acceptance)的态度，那是在1858年10月；他在一封**亲切的**(cordial)信中**向**(assuring)胡克**保证**(assuring)，自己对这一**安排**(arrangement)感到**满意**(satisfaction)。

sentences.english: In 1889 he published a lengthy exposition of the idea and entitled it Darwinism.
sentences.chinese_source: 1889年，他出版了一部**长篇的**(lengthy)**阐述**(exposition)解释这一思想，并**将**(entitled)其**命名为**(entitled)《达尔文主义》。

sentences.english: Wallace never named the theory after himself.
sentences.chinese_source: 华莱士从未**用**(named after)自己的名字**为**(named after)这一理论**命名**(named after)。

approved_summary: 达尔文1838年构想自然选择：更适应环境者存活并传下遗传性状；1844年已写成230页手稿，仍搜证未发表。
华莱士独立构想同一原理，1858年来稿几乎与达尔文一致，令达尔文担心自己的首创地位。
莱尔、胡克安排两人成果于1858年7月同场宣读；两位作者都未出席，华莱士也未参与商定办法。
论文发表初期反响冷淡；1859年《物种起源》引起轰动，首印1250册已被书商全部订购。
华莱士1858年10月事后致信认可安排；1889年又以《达尔文主义》阐述自然选择，未用自己名字命名理论。
